WIC7B-01.kills_note: precaution: 'rarely mention robbery' holds. receipt: 'gap between the rate ... was interest' holds (and receipt is off-frame for 'less a convenience than'). formality: 'discuss, at length' holds.
WIC7B-01.free_elimination: receipt is the only non-function noun in a 'less a convenience than a(n)' frame; students drop it without reading.
WIC7B-01.note: 'interest under another name, at a time when lending at interest was forbidden by the Church' is a near-gloss of evasion; the passage hands over the answer more directly than a hard item should. Key is the vivid option here.

WIC7B-02.kills_note: repairing: 'no resurfacing of that date' holds. extending: holds by placement (stones stand beside roads paved centuries earlier). commemorating: the named kill ('each new name chiselled over the last') shows emperors REPLACING predecessors, which is about the names, not the roads; 'commemorating old ones in the name of whoever happened to rule' still reads as a sentence. It loses to claiming on the whole argument, not on one sentence.
WIC7B-02.free_elimination: none; all four are road-verbs and all four take 'old ones'.
WIC7B-02.note: Best item in the batch. Consider a half-sentence that makes the appropriation explicit ('as though he had laid them') if the repair pass wants commemorating dead rather than merely weaker.

WIC7B-03.kills_note: obligation: 'when no such need remained' holds. habit: 'in several cases sharpened them' + letters that 'discuss where a part should end' hold. chance: same letters hold.
WIC7B-03.free_elimination: 'whatever it had first been for their publishers' tells the reader the answer is NOT the publishers' motive; obligation is the publishers' motive and goes without the passage. chance is a weak fourth.
WIC7B-03.note: Sound but easy: the blank sentence itself excludes obligation, and 'discuss ... in the same terms they used for where a scene should begin' is a gloss of design. Author says medium.

WIC7B-04.kills_note: ideal: 'kept whichever forms filled a line of type conveniently' holds. casualty: 'the spellings that did become fixed are the ones found in the output of ... printing houses' holds. ornament: convenience sentence holds.
WIC7B-04.free_elimination: The blank sentence alone does most of the work: 'of the trade rather than of the schoolroom ... bears the marks of the workbench, not the lecture' kills ideal and ornament without the passage; casualty is a negative singleton in a neutral frame.
WIC7B-04.note: read_aloud: the key uses artifact in the 'by-product' sense (statistical-artifact register). A student who knows only the museum sense will still land on it by elimination, so it is fair, but it is the sense-shift rather than the passage that makes the item feel hard. Author says hard; the passage is barely needed.

WIC7B-05.kills_note: protective: the blank sentence's own 'though' plus 'fines ... went to the guild rather than to any buyer' hold. advisory: 'could not then be sold legally' holds. decorative: 'The mark did guarantee the metal' holds.
WIC7B-05.free_elimination: 'and the buyer's confidence was a means to it' rules out protective in the blank sentence itself (protection would be the end, not the means); decorative and advisory are off-register. Distractor protective is a morphological echo of 'consumer protection' in sentence one.
WIC7B-05.note: Key is the vivid option and the only one the blank sentence's 'means to it' clause leaves standing. 'imported work of equal fineness was refused it' is a gloss of exclusionary. Author says hard.

WIC7B-06.kills_note: oversight: contrast with the detailed first section holds, and the trailing clause kills it again. compromise / rebuke: 'ask for particular embellishments by name' holds for both.
WIC7B-06.free_elimination: The trailing clause 'the singer who filled it was doing what the page asked' is a paraphrase of invitation: with the passage covered and only the blank sentence shown, one option is legal. Without that clause the opener 'Far from being the composer's intention' actively points to oversight, which is a good trap the author threw away.
WIC7B-06.note: Two repairs. (1) Cut or blunt the trailing clause; the letters sentence already does the killing. (2) 'Far from being the composer's intention, the bare repeat was his invitation' is internally awkward: an invitation IS an intention. Reword to 'Far from recording the composer's intention' or 'Far from being what the composer wanted heard'. Author says hard; as written it is medium at most.

WIC7B-07.kills_note: inflates: 'does not overstate literacy' holds (it is the same word). defines / ignores: 'by a margin' in the blank sentence holds for both.
WIC7B-07.free_elimination: Everything. 'does not overstate literacy ... It ______ it, and by a margin' is an antonym resolver: inflates cancels against 'does not overstate', defines and ignores cannot take 'by a margin'. One option is legal from the two local sentences alone.
WIC7B-07.note: Confirming the author's own worry: the passage is not needed. read_aloud: 'It ______ it' is an ugly double pronoun. Repair: delete the 'does not overstate ... as critics once assumed' sentence and make the blank 'The signature rate therefore ______ literacy, and by a margin larger for women than for men' so the reader must at least process 'reading was taught before writing'. Even then the item is easy (the 'Signatures therefore miss a whole class of readers' sentence is a gloss). Consider dropping. Author says medium.

WIC7B-08.kills_note: imposed: 'speakers who had no lords to please' sits in the blank sentence and holds. forgotten: sentence one holds. resisted: the named kill (beef 'names the animal as well as the meat') shows the WORD was adopted, but the option is about the PAIRING being resisted; a student can read 'the pairing was resisted over generations by speakers who had no lords to please' as 'ordinary speakers refused the split for a long time', which the two-centuries gap half-supports. It is the wrong account of how the pairing arose, but nothing says so in one sentence.
WIC7B-08.free_elimination: forgotten (the pairing is described as still taught). imposed dies inside the blank sentence. Two legal.
WIC7B-08.note: Acceptable. If the repair pass wants resisted dead, add a clause after 'names the animal as well as the meat': 'and only later narrowed to the table' -- that makes the pairing an outcome speakers arrived at, not one they fought.

WIC7B-09.kills_note: saving: 'ended the month with a small credit' holds. credit: same sentence holds, as a trap not a kill; the option in its borrowing sense is the 'keeping workers in debt' story the passage calls 'less dramatic', so it is the debunked reading. comparison: 'prices ran only a little above those in the nearest town' holds. departure is given outright by the train-ticket sentence.
WIC7B-09.free_elimination: None from the blank sentence: 'not solvency but ______' leaves all four legal. The sentence AFTER the blank resolves it in one read.
WIC7B-09.note: The credit homograph is fair, not a gotcha: it is the passage-word echo distractor, and the passage itself says families HELD credit. A student who picks it has misread the passage, not the option. Solid item; 'not solvency but departure' is slightly stiff aloud (solvency is a state, departure an act) but acceptable.

WIC7B-10.kills_note: material: 'though the block is the same stone' holds. pose: 'the same pose with a strut in one version and without it in another' holds. workmanship: there is NO killing sentence. The author's kill is 'the passage locates the value in what that carving told a visitor' -- that is the argument for the key, not a sentence against workmanship. The passage says the strut was 'carved with as much care as the figure', which a student legitimately reads as evidence that buyers paid for craftsmanship; nothing in the passage says the figure carving was indifferent or that skill was not what sold.
WIC7B-10.free_elimination: material (the frame is about what the stump 'told a visitor', a signal, not a substance). Three legal from the blank sentence.
WIC7B-10.note: REPAIR REQUIRED. Add a sentence that kills workmanship: e.g. after 'Buyers, it seems, wanted the strut.' insert 'The figures on these copies are often summary work; the strut is the one part carved with care.' -- then care on the strut cannot be read as general craftsmanship. read_aloud: 'the copy's value lay in the reference' is stilted; 'reference' without a complement is thin. Consider 'lay in the reference, not the stone' (kills material again, cleanly) or 'lay in the ______ it made to the original' with reference/claim/debt-type options.

WIC7B-11.kills_note: punishment: holds (sanctuary WAS punishing). contest: 'nearly every sanctuary-seeker was made to confess' holds. loophole: the named kill FAILS. 'For the crown this was a conviction obtained without a trial' is precisely why the completed sentence 'Sanctuary was less a loophole than a procedure' is TRUE -- it supports loophole in the X slot of the 'less X than Y' frame instead of ruling it out. The conventional reading in sentence one (fugitive escapes the gallows) can be named 'mercy'->reprieve OR 'escape from the law'->loophole; both are the discarded reading the frame asks for. Reprieve is closer to the passage's word 'mercy'; loophole is not wrong.
WIC7B-11.free_elimination: punishment (the frame wants the sentimental view; punishment is the revised view). Three legal from the blank sentence.
WIC7B-11.note: REPAIR REQUIRED: replace loophole. Candidates with a real kill: 'negotiation' (killed by 'was made to confess ... to forfeit ... forbidden to stray' -- nothing was bargained; overlaps contest, so swap contest for 'ceremony', killed by 'For the crown this was a conviction': it had legal effect) or 'penance' (killed only by absence -- weaker). Do not keep loophole. Hard for the wrong reason as written.

WIC7B-12.kills_note: rising: 'not high tolls' + the ceilings hold. hidden: 'published schedules' holds. arbitrary: the named kill FAILS. 'a rate set by statute is not capricious' describes the world AFTER the floor was granted; the sentence asks what traders FEARED, i.e. what companies would do absent the floor, and the passage says the companies wanted 'the freedom to discount' -- pricing at the company's discretion is arbitrary by any ordinary reading. Unequal is more precise (the floor text names 'one merchant ... another ... the same cargo'); arbitrary is not excluded. This is exactly the 'more precise, not exclusive' failure from the last batch.
WIC7B-12.free_elimination: rising (cancels against 'not high tolls'); hidden (published schedules are in the blank's own paragraph frame). Two-to-three legal.
WIC7B-12.note: REPAIR REQUIRED: replace arbitrary. Suggest 'uniform' -- a genuine trap (the floor is a uniformity rule) killed by a specific sentence: 'The petitions asking for the floors came from the traders themselves' (traders asked for uniformity, so they did not fear it). Alternative 'punitive' is killed by 'not high tolls' but duplicates rising.

WIC7B-13.kills_note: preview: cancels against 'not a spoiler' in the blank sentence itself. confession / joke: the household/table-of-contents sentence holds for both, and neither is 'a tool'.
WIC7B-13.free_elimination: Everything. 'not a spoiler but a(n) ______, and its clumsiness is the clumsiness of a tool seen out of its use': preview = spoiler, confession and joke are not tools, bookmark is the only tool. One legal with the passage covered.
WIC7B-13.note: Confirming the author's worry. REPAIR: delete 'of a tool seen out of its use' (e.g. end at 'a(n) ______, clumsy only to a reader who no longer needs it'). The 'find the place at which to rejoin' sentence carries the item on its own and then the passage is needed. Also 'bookmark' for a table-of-contents entry is a metaphor; 'signpost' or 'finding aid' would be more literal but bookmark is acceptable. Author says hard; as written it is easy.

WIC7B-14.kills_note: exaggerated: 'rose less' holds. invisible: 'those towns felt the shortage ... their prices rose less' holds -- the famine registers, softened -- but a student anchored on 'recorded nothing at all' and on the tail 'precisely because they were the worst' (which reads naturally with invisible: worst -> empty markets -> nothing recorded) will pick it; the kill is the third logical step and the passage makes it in a subordinate clause. delayed: no kill, unsupported only; the author concedes this.
WIC7B-14.free_elimination: None from the blank sentence; delayed is the weakest but 'delayed in the record' is a legal phrase. Four legal.
WIC7B-14.note: Acceptable as is; the muted/invisible discrimination is the item's real work and the passage does support it. If the repair pass wants delayed to have a kill, 'localized' does not work either; leave delayed -- one unsupported distractor per item is normal SAT practice and the other three are killed.
